pass_a_gloss: When therefore Greeks were under sin as having been ignorant of the Creator, and Jews as liable for the transgression of the law, there was need, of necessity, for those being on the earth of the Christ who justifies; for we have been justified not from works in righteousness which we did, but according to his much mercy; for he himself was the one who also of old was saying through voice of prophets: I am the one wiping out your lawlessnesses, and I will not remember. And the justifying grace darts through into all equally, Jews I mean and Greeks, because all both sinned and lack the glory of God; and glory of God would fittingly be understood: neither to know nor to be of a nature to err; and behind, wholly, the boasts of the Godhead is all the created creation; for some of the angels too slipped aside. However the God and Father was well pleased to sum up all things in the Christ who justifies as a gift by his grace; for he has been set as a propitiation through faith in his blood; for since he made his own blood the exchange for the life of all, he saved the [world] under heaven, and set the Father and God in the heavens gracious and well disposed toward us. Where then the boasting? It was shut out. For who at all, or upon what things, will boast, all having become useless and having bent away from the straight road, and there being entirely no one doing kindness? Therefore the boasting was shut out, he says, that is, it has been thrown out and taken away, having no place at all with us; and it was shut out in what manner? We have been enriched with the passing over of the sins done before, being justified by mercy and grace as a gift in Christ. Do we then make law idle through faith? The God of the whole said to the divine Moses: A prophet for them I will raise up from their brothers like you, and I will give my word in his mouth, and he will speak to them just as I command him; and that man, whoever does not hear his words, as many as the prophet speaks upon my name, I will exact vengeance from him. How then do we not set up law through the faith, admitting the word from him? And Emmanuel has been named prophet because of the human, the one who, as in the rank of Moses, is go-between of God and men. And again, the law was in shadows, but it is seen to be in birth-pangs with the shaping of the truth; and the truth does not take away the types, but sets them down more visible. For if Abraham was justified from works, he has a boast, but not toward God. And it is needful, I suppose, someone said, that those busying themselves about the account concerning the forefather Abraham say that thing: it has been said somewhere by one of the holy disciples that apart from the works the faith is dead; and he brings on to these: But do you wish to know, O empty man, that the faith without the works is dead? pass_b_english: When, then, the Greeks were under sin for not knowing the Creator, and the Jews as guilty of transgressing the law, those on the earth necessarily had need of Christ, who justifies. For we have been justified “not by works of righteousness that we have done, but according to his great mercy” (Titus 3:5). For it was he who long ago said through the voice of the prophets, “I am he who blots out your transgressions, and I will not remember them” (Isaiah 43:25). Justifying grace passes to all alike, I mean to Jews and Greeks, because “all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God” (Romans 3:23). The glory of God may fittingly be understood as this: neither to know how to do wrong nor to be of a nature that can do wrong. And the whole created order surely falls short of the glories of the Godhead, for even some of the angels slipped. Yet God the Father was pleased “to sum up all things in Christ” (Ephesians 1:10), who justifies freely by his grace (Romans 3:24). For he has been set forth as a propitiation through faith in his blood (Romans 3:25). Since he made his own blood the price given in exchange for the life of all, he has saved the world under heaven and made the Father and God in heaven merciful and kindly toward us.

“Where then is boasting? It is excluded” (Romans 3:27). For who at all will boast, or in what, when all have become worthless and turned aside from the straight way, and there is no one at all who does good (Psalm 14:3; Romans 3:12)? So, he says, boasting is excluded; that is, it has been thrown out and done away with, and has no place at all among us. And how was it excluded? We have been enriched with the forgiveness of sins committed before (Romans 3:25), being justified freely, by mercy and grace, in Christ.

“Do we then nullify the law through faith?” (Romans 3:31). The God of all said to the inspired Moses: “I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their brothers, and I will put my word in his mouth, and he will speak to them whatever I command him. And the man who does not listen to his words, whatever the prophet speaks in my name, I will take vengeance on him” (Deuteronomy 18:18–19). How then do we not uphold the law through faith, when we receive the word that comes from him? Emmanuel has been called a prophet because of his humanity, standing, as it were, in the place of Moses as mediator between God and men (1 Timothy 2:5). And again, the law was in shadows, yet it is seen to be in labor with the form of the truth; and the truth does not abolish the types but makes them clearer.

“For if Abraham was justified by works, he has something to boast about, but not before God” (Romans 4:2). I think, someone has said, that those who look closely into the account of our forefather Abraham ought to say this: it has been said somewhere by one of the holy disciples that faith without works is dead (James 2:26). revisions.summary: Pass A, lemmas, choices and bible_refs rebuilt from the Greek to match the reviewed English; pass_b_english is the current English.

review_notes: Old draft had serious errors: 'neither comes from knowing nor from being born to sin' for the definition of God's glory (μήτε εἰδέναι μήτε πεφυκέναι πλημμελεῖν; the stray μή in PG is read by sense); 'every created thing is subject to the exaltations of divinity, for we have slipped' where Greek says creation falls short of the Godhead's glories because even some angels slipped; 'all are in need' and 'no one completely does good' for ἠχρειωμένων and οὐδενὸς … τοῦ ποιοῦντος χρηστότητα; an added 'Certainly not!' after Romans 3:31; and a reversed subject ('this prophet is called Emmanuel') where Greek says Emmanuel is called a prophet. It also carried no inline citations for Titus 3:5, Isaiah 43:25, Romans 3:23-27, Ephesians 1:10, Deuteronomy 18:18-19, 1 Timothy 2:5, Romans 4:2, James 2:20, 2:26. The 'someone has said' (ἔφη τις) speaker is kept; χρῆναι as 'ought to'. Edge cut at 'ἐπὶ τὸ' marked with an ellipsis. Old translator_notes are worksheet debris and should be dropped.
μήτε εἰδέναι μήτε πεφυκέναι πλημμελεῖν: a stray μή in the printed text is read by sense.
